[[James Belich (historian)|James Belich]] (uncle) | profession = Lawyer | spouse = [[Andrew Kirton]] | children = 3 | website = | footnotes = }} '''Camilla Vera Feslier Belich'''{{Cite web|url=https://www.parliament.nz/en/pb/hansard-debates/rhr/document/HansS_20201125_039660000/event|title=Event – New Zealand Parliament|website=www.parliament.nz}} is a New Zealand lawyer, trade unionist and politician. She has been a [[Member of parliament|Member of Parliament]], representing the [[New Zealand Labour Party]], since 2020. ==Early life and family== Belich was raised in Wellington, where her grandfather [[Jim Belich|Sir Jim Belich]] was [[Mayor of Wellington|mayor]] from 1986 to 1992. Her parents were trade unionists.{{Cite web |last=Belich |first=Camilla |date=3 December 2020 |title=Maiden statement |url=https://www.parliament.nz/en/pb/hansard-debates/rhr/document/HansS_20201203_051960000/belich-camilla |access-date=22 January 2024 |website=New Zealand Parliament}} As a teenager, Belich attended [[Wellington East Girls' College]] and was a member of the Wellington City Youth Council.{{Cite news |last=Ryan |first=Jenny |date=5 August 2000 |title=Stand-in MP expects 'kinda cool' session |work=[[The Dominion (Wellington)|The Dominion]] |pages=2}} While in the seventh form, she was selected to represent [[Rongotai (New Zealand electorate)|Rongotai]] MP [[Annette King]] as a member of the third [[New Zealand Youth Parliament]] in 2000.{{cite web |last=Harré |first=Laila |date=2000-07-06 |title=Youth Parliament to debate decriminalisation |url=http://www.beehive.govt.nz/release/youth-parliament-debate-decriminalisation |access-date=2021-05-26 |website=beehive.govt.nz}} She would go on to be one of six former youth MPs to be members of Parliament in 2021.{{Cite web |date=2021-10-05 |title=From Youth MPs to actual MPs |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/national/programmes/the-house/audio/2018815120/from-youth-mps-to-actual-mps |access-date=2024-01-22 |website=[[RNZ]] |language=en-nz}} Belich studied [[Māori language|te reo Māori]] and law at [[Victoria University of Wellington]]. She became involved in student politics and was co-president of the [[New Zealand University Students Association]] with [[Andrew Kirton]], her future husband, in 2005.{{Cite web |title=About Us |url=https://www.students.org.nz/about-us |access-date=2024-01-22 |website=New Zealand Union of Students' Associations |language=en-US}}{{cite news |date=5 March 2021 |title=Beehive Diaries: A lockdown baby for new MP, Ashley Bloomfield's dance moves |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/politics/beehive-diaries-a-lockdown-baby-for-new-mp-ashley-bloomfields-dance-moves/5AHH2HCRPSZ5KBB2LPP2C3W5TA/ |url-access=subscription |newspaper=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |quote=New Labour MP Camilla Belich has had a baby boy}} Kirton and Belich have three children, the third of whom was born after Belich was elected to Parliament. == Legal career == Belich has worked as an employment lawyer, beginning her career at Oakley Moran, a [[Wellington]] law firm, before moving to [[London]] in 2009 where she worked for a law firm and later for [[Unison (trade union)|Unison]], the largest trade union in the United Kingdom between 2012 and 2016.{{cite news |date=18 October 2020 |title=The 40 diverse new MPs entering Parliament |url=https://www.newstalkzb.co.nz/news/vote-2020/election-2020-the-forty-newcomers-entering-parliament/ |access-date=20 October 2020 |publisher=[[Newstalk ZB]]}} There, she won acclaim for her role in winning a high-profile case in the [[Court of Justice of the European Union]] about safe working hours.{{cite news |last1=Amelia |first1=Wade |title=Labour Party's latest candidate to contest key Epsom seat |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=12334288 |access-date=15 June 2020 |publisher=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |date=24 May 2020}} Returning to New Zealand, she joined the Wellington employment law firm Bartlett Law as a senior associate in 2017.{{cite news |date=7 March 2017 |title=Camilla Belich joins Bartlett Law |url=https://www.lawsociety.org.nz/news/newsroom/recent-movements/camilla-belich-joins-bartlett-law2/ |access-date=22 January 2024 |publisher=[[New Zealand Law Society]]}} She specialised in employment discrimination cases. She also worked for unions in New Zealand as a barrister and solicitor, firstly on equal pay issues at the [[New Zealand Council of Trade Unions]] until 2019, and subsequently for the [[Public Service Association]] in Auckland. == Member of Parliament == {{NZ parlbox header|align=left}} {{NZ parlbox|term=53rd |start = [[2020 New Zealand general election|2020]] |end=2023 |electorate=List |party=New Zealand Labour Party |list=30 }} {{NZ parlbox break}} {{NZ parlbox |term=54th |start=2023 |end=present |list=26 |party=New Zealand Labour Party |electorate=List }} {{End}} ===First term, 2020–2023=== Belich was considered as a possible Labour candidate in [[Rongotai (New Zealand electorate)|Rongotai]] for the [[2017 New Zealand general election|2017 general election]].{{Cite web |last=Moir |first=Jo |date=2022-05-10 |title=Eagle's Rongotai exit paves way for ex-councillor |url=http://newsroom.co.nz/2022/05/10/eagles-rongotai-exit-paves-way-for-another-ex-councillor/ |access-date=2024-01-22 |website=Newsroom |language=en-US}} She was selected as a Labour candidate in the [[2020 New Zealand general election|2020 general election]]. She ran for the electorate of {{NZ electorate link|Epsom}}, finishing second, but became an MP based on her ranking of 30th on the Labour [[party list]].{{cite news |author=Coughlan, Thomas |title=Ayesha Verrall leads fresh-faced Labour party list for 2020 |work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/300034942/ayesha-verrall-leads-freshfaced-labour-party-list-for-2020 |access-date=15 June 2020 |date=15 June 2020 }}{{cite web |title=Epsom – Official Result|url=https://electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2020/electorate-details-11.html |publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]] |access-date=23 October 2020 }}{{cite web |title=2020 General Election and Referendums – Official Result Successful Candidates |url=https://electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2020/successful-candidates.html |publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]] |access-date=5 February 2021 |url-status=dead |archive-date=7 November 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201107204759/https://electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2020/successful-candidates.html }} In her first term, she was the deputy chair of the education and workforce select committee until 2023 when she became the chair of the committee as well as a junior government [[Whip (politics)|whip]].{{cite news |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/politics/inside-the-labour-battle-over-jacinda-arderns-mt-albert-seat/EPDYMXOHTFEZ7FMDJBPHVV4W5Q/ |first=Audrey |last=Young |title=Inside the Labour battle over Jacinda Ardern's Mt Albert seat |website=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |date=9 March 2023 |access-date=11 March 2023 |url-access=subscription }} In 2023, Belich inherited [[Duncan Webb]]'s private members bill, the Companies (Directors Duties) Amendment Bill, which amended the [[Companies Act 1993]] to remove doubt that company directors may consider matters other than maximising profit, such as [[environmental, social, and corporate governance]] and [[Treaty of Waitangi]] considerations, when discharging their duties.{{Cite web |date=2024-01-30 |title=Companies (Directors Duties) Amendment Bill — Second Reading - New Zealand Parliament |url=https://www.parliament.nz/en/pb/hansard-debates/rhr/combined/HansDeb_20230607_20230607_40 |access-date=2024-01-22 |website=www.parliament.nz |language=en}} The bill was described as "controversial" because it failed to receive select committee support, was perceived to increase the risk of litigation for companies and directors, and because it imposed no new obligations.{{Cite web |title=Simpson Grierson - Controversial change to directors' duties passes |url=https://www.simpsongrierson.com/insights-news/legal-updates/controversial-change-to-directors-duties-passes |access-date=2024-01-22 |website=www.simpsongrierson.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=The Companies (Directors' Duties) Amendment Bill has received Royal assent and has become law |url=https://www.al.nz/the-companies-directors-duties-amendment-bill-has-received-royal-assent-and-has-become-law/#:~:text=The%20substance%20of%20the%20Bill,best%20interest%20of%20the%20company. |access-date=2024-01-22 |website=www.al.nz | date=10 August 2023 |language=en-US}} Nonetheless, it passed its third reading on 1 August 2023 with Belich saying in the debate that the bill started from a misunderstanding that business must be profitable at all costs and that the bill, in its final draft, provided clarity to avoid future misunderstandings about company law.{{Cite web |date=2024-01-30 |title=Companies (Directors' Duties) Amendment Bill — Third Reading - New Zealand Parliament |url=https://www.parliament.nz/en/pb/hansard-debates/rhr/combined/HansDeb_20230801_20230802_04 |access-date=2024-01-22 |website=www.parliament.nz |language=en}} Ahead of the [[2023 New Zealand general election|2023 general election]], Belich sought to succeed retiring former prime minister [[Jacinda Ardern]] in the safe Labour electorate of {{NZ electorate link|Mount Albert}}. Despite having Ardern's personal support,{{Cite web |date=2023-03-19 |title=Labour chooses candidate to replace Grant Robertson |url=https://www.odt.co.nz/star-news/star-national/labour-chooses-candidate-replace-grant-robertson |access-date=2024-01-22 |website=[[Otago Daily Times]] |language=en}} Belich missed out with fellow list MP [[Helen White (politician)|Helen White]] winning the selection.{{cite news |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/300827886/labour-selects-helen-white-to-replace-jacinda-ardern-in-mt-albert-seat |first=Erin |last=Johnson |title=Labour selects Helen White to replace Jacinda Ardern in Mt Albert seat |website=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |date=11 March 2023 |access-date=11 March 2023 }} She was later re-selected as Labour's candidate in [[Epsom (New Zealand electorate)|Epsom]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/politics/election-2023-promising-labour-mp-chosen-as-candidate-in-aucklands-epsom-electorate/N4SIHXI4LVE4LNDNAKVTIU25SA/|title=Promising Labour MP chosen as candidate in Auckland's Epsom electorate|date=22 May 2023|website=[[The New Zealand Herald]] }} ===Second term, 2023–present=== Belich was briefly unseated after the election. She placed third in [[Epsom (New Zealand electorate)|Epsom]], and her [[Party lists in the 2023 New Zealand general election#Labour Party|list placement]] of 26 meant she was the first list candidate not to be elected after the official results were announced. However, senior Labour MP [[Andrew Little (New Zealand politician)|Andrew Little]] opted not to take up his list seat and formally resigned from the House on 5 December. This resulted in Belich's election as a list MP to replace Little the following day.{{cite web |title=Epsom – Official Result |url=https://archive.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2023/electorate-details-11.html |publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]] |access-date=24 November 2023 |date=3 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231205003234/https://archive.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2023/electorate-details-11.html|archive-date=5 December 2023|url-status=live}}{{cite news |url=https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2310/S00088/andrew-little-to-retire-from-politics.htm |title=Andrew Little To Retire From Politics |website=[[Scoop (website)|Scoop]] |date=17 October 2023 |access-date=9 November 2023 }}{{cite news |url=https://gazette.govt.nz/notice/id/2023-au5688 |title=Declaration by Electoral Commission that Camilla Vera Feslier Belich is elected a Member of Parliament |date=6 December 2023 |work=[[New Zealand Gazette]] |access-date=8 December 2023}} She assumed the junior whip, workplace relations and safety, and emergency management portfolios in the [[Shadow Cabinet of Chris Hipkins]].{{cite news |title=Labour Party leader Chris Hipkins reveals new shadow Cabinet |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/503581/labour-party-leader-chris-hipkins-reveals-new-shadow-cabinet#:~:text=The%20full%20line%2Dup%3A,Grant%20Robertson%20%2D%20Finance%2C%20Racing |access-date=19 December 2023 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=30 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231211134745/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/503581/labour-party-leader-chris-hipkins-reveals-new-shadow-cabinet#:~:text=The%20full%20line%2Dup%3A,Grant%20Robertson%20%2D%20Finance%2C%20Racing |archive-date=11 December 2023|url-status=live}} On 7 March 2025, Belich was allocated the [[Accident Compensation Corporation]] (ACC) and public services portfolios during a shadow [[cabinet reshuffle]]. She retained the emergency management portfolio but lost the workplace relations and safety portfolio, and a short time later left the whips team.{{cite news |last1=Palmer |first1=Russell |title=Chris Hipkins announces new Labour 'economic team', Tangi Utikere promoted |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/544048/chris-hipkins-announces-new-labour-economic-team-tangi-utikere-promoted |access-date=8 March 2025 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=7 March 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250307011659/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/544048/chris-hipkins-announces-new-labour-economic-team-tangi-utikere-promoted |archive-date=7 March 2025}}{{cite news |last=McConnell |first=Glenn |title=Labour MP gets $53,000 pay cut for 'promotion' |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/politics/360612783/labour-mp-gets-53000-pay-cut-promotion |access-date=13 March 2025 |website=Stuff}} In late 2023, Belich inherited a member's bill previously in the name of [[Ibrahim Omer]], who had been defeated in that year's election. The Crimes (Theft By Employer) Amendment Bill is intended to clarify that an employer withholding an employees' wages is theft and had passed its first reading while Labour was in government. Despite the change of government, and although a select committee had not recommended the bill pass, [[New Zealand First]] voted with the opposition parties to pass the bill through its third reading on 12 March 2025. The bill received royal assent on 13 March.{{cite news |last=Palmer |first=Russell |date=13 March 2025 |title=Bill making employers theft of workers' wages a crime passes |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/544621/theft-is-theft-bill-making-employers-theft-of-workers-wages-a-crime-passes |access-date=13 March 2025 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250312203048/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/544621/theft-is-theft-bill-making-employers-theft-of-workers-wages-a-crime-passes|archive-date=12 March 2025|url-status=live}} Another member's bill in Belich's name, the Employment Relations (Employee Remuneration Disclosure) Amendment Bill, passed its first reading in November 2024 with support from the opposition and National. The bill proposes to prohibit employers from taking disciplinary action against employees who disclose their remuneration to their colleagues.{{Cite web |date=6 November 2024 |title=Employment Relations (Employee Remuneration Disclosure) Amendment Bill — First Reading |url=https://www.parliament.nz/en/pb/hansard-debates/rhr/combined/HansDeb_20241106_20241106_48 |access-date=19 March 2025 |website=New Zealand Parliament}}{{cite news |last=Stock |first=Rob |title=The right to tell your colleagues what you are paid |url=https://www.thepost.co.nz/business/360617954/right-tell-your-colleagues-what-you-are-paid |access-date=18 March 2025 |website=The Post}} On 20 August 2025, Belich's bill banning employers from imposing gag orders on workers talking about their salaries passed into law with the support of the [[Green Party of Aotearoa New Zealand|Green]], [[Te Pāti Māori|Māori]], and [[New Zealand National Party|National]] parties. The [[New Zealand First]] and [[ACT New Zealand|ACT]] parties opposed the legislation.{{cite news |last1=Hanly |first1=Lillian |title=Two Labour bills pass into law |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/national/570603/two-labour-bills-pass-into-law |access-date=21 August 2025 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=21 August 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250821010442/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/national/570603/two-labour-bills-pass-into-law |archive-date=21 August 2025 |url-status=live}} Following a cabinet reshuffle on 11 March 2026, Belich gained the justice portfolio.{{cite news |last1=Ricketts |first1=Emma |title=Hipkins reshuffles Labour portfolios as Henare departs, and plan hatched for Maori seats |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/politics/360949687/hipkins-reshuffles-labour-portfolios-henare-departs-and-plan-hatched-maori-seats-race |work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |access-date=11 March 2026 |date=11 March 2026 |url-status=live}} In late January 2026, Belich and National Party MP [[Greg Fleming (politician)|Greg Fleming]] co-sponsored a [[modern slavery]] bill that proposes fining large companies NZ$200,000 for failing to monitor and report modern slavery in their supply chain. Due to the [[ACT New Zealand|ACT Party]] and [[Minister for Workplace Relations]] [[Brooke van Velden]]'s objections, the duo decided to co-sponsor the member's bill to circumvent the private member's bill ballot system.{{cite news |title=Watch: National and Labour MPs team up to get slavery bill heard after ACT objects |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/585319/watch-national-and-labour-mps-team-up-to-get-slavery-bill-heard-after-act-objects |access-date=9 May 2026 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=29 January 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260421222705/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/585319/watch-national-and-labour-mps-team-up-to-get-slavery-bill-heard-after-act-objects |archive-date=21 April 2026 |url-status=live}} The bill passed its first reading on 29 April 2026 with the support of all parliamentary parties except ACT.{{cite news |last1=Palmer |first1=Russell |title=Modern Slavery bill passes first reading under new Parliament rule |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/593743/modern-slavery-bill-passes-first-reading-under-new-parliament-rule |access-date=9 May 2026 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=29 April 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260429061755/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/593743/modern-slavery-bill-passes-first-reading-under-new-parliament-rule |archive-date=29 April 2026
